title: Visual Basic
subtitle: The readable, English-like language that brought programming to millions of Windows developers: Visual Basic .NET today, and how to maintain and migrate the code it left behind.
description: Visual Basic is one of the most influential languages in the history of personal computing. Classic Visual Basic, released by Microsoft in 1991, let people build Windows applications by drawing forms and writing short pieces of BASIC code behind buttons, and through the 1990s it was one of the most popular ways to build Windows software. In 2002 it was redesigned as Visual Basic .NET, a fully object-oriented language on .NET that compiles to the same code as C#. Its sibling, VBA (Visual Basic for Applications), still automates Microsoft Office. Microsoft supports Visual Basic on modern .NET, mainly for Windows desktop applications, class libraries and console programs, but has said that it will not evolve the language further: its design is stable, and new .NET features are made usable from it without new syntax.

This course is for anyone who has finished the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or has equivalent experience, and especially for those who will maintain, modernise or migrate Visual Basic code: a very large amount of it still runs businesses, laboratories and public services. In eight lessons it covers the history and present status of the language, modules and `Sub Main`, variables and types, control flow, procedures and functions, classes, collections and LINQ, files, text formatting and asynchronous code, error handling, and how professionals maintain and migrate Visual Basic code, including the move from Visual Basic 6 and to C#, ending with a complete program and where to go next.

To run the examples, install the .NET 10 SDK from the [official download page](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download), create a project with `dotnet new console -lang VB`, replace its `Program.vb` with an example, and run `dotnet run`. There is no official online playground; the community site [.NET Fiddle](https://dotnetfiddle.net/) can run Visual Basic .NET in the browser. Every complete Visual Basic program in these lessons was compiled and run as a console project with the .NET 10 SDK (whose Visual Basic compiler defaults to language version 17.13), and the one C# program, used for comparison in the migration lesson, was run with the same SDK; the output shown is the output each printed.

levels.title: The language
levels.summary: Where Visual Basic came from and where it stands today, how a program is laid out in modules with Sub Main, and the types, operators and control flow of everyday code.

levels.title: Building programs
levels.summary: Organise code into procedures and functions, model data with classes, properties, interfaces and events, process data with collections and LINQ, and work with files, text and asynchronous input and output.

levels.title: Living with Visual Basic code
levels.summary: Handle errors in modern and legacy styles, maintain, upgrade and migrate Visual Basic codebases the way professionals do, and build a complete, tested program.
